newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- China's total imports and exports this year could be expected to reach US$310 billion, up 6.4 per cent from 1996.
-- A series of activities aimed at promoting the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Basic Law would be held in Guangdong province.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Red chip companies have raised more than HK$10 billion in the past three months, but analysts said the purpose for most of the fund raising was not apparent.

-- MING PAO -- The close relationship between the former director of immigration, Laurence Leung, and pro-Beijing businessman Tsui Tsin-tong would be the focus of the next Legislative Council inquiry over Leung's early retirement.

-- Beijing has issued internal instructions stressing again that the Chinese media should unify terms used for covering the Hong Kong handover. According to the instructions, Hong Kong cannot be described as a "British colony".

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Governor Chris Patten warned that proposals by the China-appointed Preparatory Committee to dilute some Hong Kong human rights laws struck at the heart of the territory's civil liberties.
-- China planned to set up a timetable and a marketmaker system for Treasury bond sales this year to cut funding costs and improve liquidity in the secondary debt market.
-- Analysts said China's dominant phone company, China Telecom, could be on the verge of taking a more active role in the territory.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Cosco Pacific was focusing on the global expansion of its core container leasing, terminal operation and manufacturing businesses.
-- China's major state banks reported profits last year, and analysts said this showed they were beginning to act like commercial banks elsewhere.
